title: Mission Match Board
one_liner: Paste your prize mission and a list of prospect bios to get a ranked list of who has publicly said they care about your goal.
speaker: Peter Diamandis
context: Peter's space prize was turned down at least 150 times over about four and a half years. He finally found his sponsor by reading a magazine list of wealthy young women, where one profile said she wanted to fly suborbital.
demo: The organizer types a short mission description and pastes prospect profiles, one per block (name plus bio or interview text they collected). The tool pulls out goal phrases and scores each prospect on overlap with the mission's keywords and synonyms. It shows the matching sentences highlighted and ranks the list. Each prospect gets a draft outreach angle, either from a template or using the visitor's own pasted AI key, and the result exports as CSV.
data_plan: Mission text and prospect profiles come from the customer. Bundled example profiles are clearly marked fictional. AI drafting only works with a key the visitor pastes in. Without one, example mode uses template drafts.
risks: Rich prospects are hard to reach even when they match well, so results depend on the client's outreach. There are privacy and ethics questions in profiling individuals, so stick to their public statements. Clients may judge the service only on dollars raised. The '150 times' figure is one anecdote, not market data.

opportunity.title: Stated-Goal Sponsor Finder
opportunity.one_liner: Research service that finds wealthy individuals and companies whose public statements match a prize, challenge or event's mission.
opportunity.customer: Small nonprofits, foundations and organizers of incentive prizes, hackathons, student competitions and challenge grants in the US who have no full-time development staff
opportunity.problem: Organizers send the same pitch to generic lists of rich people and corporations, and nearly all of them say no. What they need is the few prospects who have said in public that they care about this exact goal. Finding them takes slow manual reading of profiles, interviews and filings.
opportunity.revenue_model: Fixed-fee prospect sprint, about $1,500–$3,000 for a ranked list of 25 matched prospects with evidence quotes and outreach angles (estimate). Optional monthly refresh at about $300 (estimate).
opportunity.why_now: The episode shows that the winning match came from a specific stated goal, not from wealth alone. AI research agents can now read hundreds of public profiles and interviews cheaply and pull out stated goals with sources, which used to take a development team weeks.
